properties: Unmount disposes one renderer; late initialization cannot resurrect it; reload attempts stay bounded; GPU restoration repaints a sleeping renderer and defers while hidden; capture receipts require current committed owner/revision/viewport, assets, semantic layout and a painted draw
assessment: actual resource lifetime and unmount/late-init evidence; DOM/GPU assumptions stay explicit
remaining: GPU/browser/URL behavior requires the actual implementation; arbitrary device/driver failure schedules are excluded.
evidenceDecision: Capture aborts revision-owned resource waiters on invalidation/deadline and recovers without settling obsolete assets. Capture uses finite injected asset/frame/deadline schedules and the production Town/Board/Desk browser consumer in BoardView.test.ts (controlled slow assets/fonts, same-topology resize, view replacement, valid empty scenes, missing/blank output, screenshot-time invalidation and never-ready no-artifact failure). No maintained model covers GPU paint or browser font/layout; existing lifecycle consumers and work ceilings remain mandatory. The HostsFilter town-idle-draws case exercises native WEBGL_lose_context loss/restoration on the production Pixi renderer at desktop and phone widths with controlled visibility and the test clock: recovery paints once after sleep, remains pending while hidden, resumes once when visible and returns to zero idle draws; a restoration event after disposal cannot draw. The Town renderer browser test (StrictMode double mount leaves one renderer and canvas; unmount leaves none) and the lazy-module tests exercise graphics destruction and reload/lifetime behavior. Committed building-sign lifecycle fixtures cover cold commit, ref stability across status renders, cull/remount, suspended uncommitted nodes and replacement-safe cleanup. Maintained phone/wide browser cases require visible building/reception recovery after cold mount and camera culling with normal roof fading; their execution and the production suites' runner-independent work ceilings remain closing browser acceptance; input-delay timing is reported by the non-blocking World latency trend (same-CPU comparison with main) and is not a pass/fail claim.
